# You're inside a real Keepance workspace

This whole thing is running in your browser. No install, no account, nothing saved to a server. It's a pretend client household for a financial advisor, pre-loaded so you can actually poke around instead of staring at an empty screen.

Everything here is a real Keepance surface. The files are real files. The editor is the real editor. The AI sidebar talks to a real model.

## What to try

1. Open `Webb Household/Review Notes.md` and read the notes the way an advisor actually keeps them after a meeting.
2. Open `Webb Household/Plan review.aichat` to watch a saved AI conversation play back, the kind that catches a stale beneficiary form before it becomes a problem.
3. Open the AI sidebar and ask it something about the open file. The demo uses a shared, rate-limited key.
4. Hit a limit? Paste your own Anthropic key for unlimited use, or download the app.

Here's the part that matters. On your own machine, these files live in a folder you pick, and your API key goes straight from your computer to the model. Nothing routes through a server I control. That's the whole point of Keepance, and it's why an advisor can use it on real client data.

Refresh the page and the workspace comes back to where it started.

# Financial Plan Summary: Webb Household

**Clients:** Marcus Webb (38) and Tanya Webb (37)
**Dependents:** Caleb (8), Ava (5)
**Goals:** Retire at 60, fund both kids' college, pay off the house early
**Risk profile:** Moderate growth (completed questionnaire, March 2026)

## Where things stand

- **Marcus 401(k):** $412,000, contributing 12% plus a 4% match. Old employer 401(k) of $96,000 still sitting at the prior custodian, not yet rolled over.
- **Tanya 403(b):** $188,000, contributing 9%.
- **Joint brokerage:** $145,000, mostly index funds.
- **Roth IRAs:** $61,000 (Marcus), $54,000 (Tanya).
- **529 plans:** $48,000 (Caleb), $29,000 (Ava).
- **Cash reserve:** $55,000 (about 5 months of expenses).
- **Mortgage:** $318,000 at 5.1%, 26 years left.

## The plan, in one paragraph

Roll the old 401(k) into Marcus's IRA so it's managed alongside everything else. Keep both kids' 529s on the current monthly auto-contribution. Revisit a Roth conversion in a low-income year. Hold the moderate-growth allocation; rebalance once a year. Do not pay down the mortgage faster yet, the retirement runway matters more right now.

## Open items

- Confirm the rollover paperwork and the receiving account.
- Recheck beneficiary designations across every account (see the beneficiary file).
- Decide on the Roth conversion amount before year-end.

# Review Notes: Webb Household

**Meeting:** Annual review
**Date:** June 12, 2026
**Present:** Marcus and Tanya Webb, me

Rough notes taken during the review. Clean up and file the action items.

## What they told me

- Marcus changed jobs last year. The $96k from the old employer 401(k) is still at the prior custodian. He wants it "in one place."
- They want to talk through the 401(k) rollover and Caleb's 529 (his words from the email).
- Tanya got a raise. They can push another $400/month into savings.
- They are nervous about the market and asked, again, whether they should move to cash. Walked them through the moderate-growth plan and the time horizon. They felt better.
- Marcus mentioned, almost in passing, that he and his first wife divorced in 2019 and he "updated everything." Worth verifying.

## What we agreed to do

- Roll the old 401(k) into Marcus's IRA. I'll start the paperwork.
- Increase the joint brokerage auto-contribution by $400/month.
- Revisit the Roth conversion before December.
- Recheck every beneficiary designation. Marcus's comment about the divorce is exactly why.

## My flags

- The old 401(k) rollover is the priority, it's been sitting too long.
- Verify beneficiaries personally. "I updated everything" after a divorce is the single most common place a household has a stale form. Do not take it on faith.

# Beneficiary Designations: Webb Household

Working record. Each account gets a row. Confirm against the custodian's record on file, do not rely on what the client remembers.

| Account | Owner | Primary beneficiary | Contingent | Last confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 401(k) (current employer) | Marcus | Tanya Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | 2026-01 |
| Old 401(k) (prior employer) | Marcus | **Jessica Reyes (100%)** | none listed | 2019 |
| 403(b) | Tanya | Marcus Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | 2026-01 |
| Roth IRA | Marcus | Tanya Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | 2026-01 |
| Roth IRA | Tanya | Marcus Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | 2026-01 |
| Joint brokerage (TOD) | Marcus & Tanya | each other | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | 2026-01 |

Notes:

- The old 401(k) still lists **Jessica Reyes**, Marcus's first wife, as the sole primary beneficiary, dated 2019. Marcus believes he "updated everything" after the divorce. He did not update this one. If he died before the rollover, that account would pass to his ex-spouse, not to Tanya.
- This is the whole reason the rollover matters beyond convenience. Roll it into the IRA and the IRA's correct beneficiaries control.
- Confirm every row against the custodian, not the client's memory.

# Client Intake Summary

**Household:** Marcus & Tanya Webb
**Relationship:** Married, two minor children
**Engagement:** Comprehensive financial planning + ongoing investment management
**Date opened:** 2025-09-04

## What the clients want

Retire by 60, get both kids through college without loans, and stop worrying every time the market dips. They want one place that sees the whole picture instead of five logins.

## Accounts under advisement

Marcus 401(k), Marcus old 401(k) (rollover pending), Tanya 403(b), two Roth IRAs, joint brokerage, two 529 plans. Mortgage and cash reserve tracked but not managed.

## Key facts to verify

- Beneficiary designation on the old 401(k) (see the beneficiary file).
- The receiving account and paperwork for the rollover.
- Current contribution rates after Tanya's raise.

## Note

This is a planning record, not tax or legal advice. Coordinate the Roth conversion timing with their CPA before executing.

# About this demo

This is the in-browser version of Keepance. It runs the same editor, file tree, and AI chat the desktop app uses, just pre-loaded with a fictional client household so you have something to look at.

The household, the names, and the numbers are all made up for illustration. Nothing here is financial advice, and the AI's job in the real app is to produce a first draft you review, not to make recommendations on its own.

What's different from the real app: this demo uses a shared, rate-limited key so you can try the AI without setting anything up. On your own machine you bring your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or a local model through Ollama), and your files and your key never leave your computer.

When you're ready, download the 30-day trial at keepance.com.
